title: Network Delay Time
signature: int Solve(int[][] times, int n, int k)
statement: Nodes are numbered 1 to n. Each entry [u, v, w] is a one-way link from u to v taking w time. A signal starts at node k. Return the time for every node to receive it, that is the largest of the shortest arrival times, or -1 if some node never receives it.
constraints: edges are DIRECTED and weights are positive
hints: Breadth-first search finds the fewest hops, which is not the same as the least time once edges have different weights. You need shortest paths by weight.
Dijkstra: keep the best known arrival time per node, always expand the unvisited node with the smallest one, and relax its outgoing edges.

A PriorityQueue of (node, time) does the choosing. Two things to get right: skip an entry when you pop it and it is already worse than the recorded best, and answer -1 if any node is still at infinity. Watch the 1-based numbering against 0-based arrays.

cases.name: a longer direct edge loses to two short ones
cycle does not trap the search
